page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a general-purpose, memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical Intel core using hyperthreading. The server features an x86_64 architecture with an allocation of 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local storage is not included, meaning persistent block storage must be provisioned externally over the network. The instance includes 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses and operates without dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

The CPU includes hardware vector and matrix acceleration support, featuring AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and Intel AMX instructions (amx_tile and amx_int8), alongside standard cryptographic flags like AES and SHA_NI. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded performance, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1640.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 1554.59. Conversely, multithreaded capacity is constrained by the 2-vCPU configuration, resulting in a Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0 and poor relative marks in code compilation, ray tracing, and physics simulations.

Memory performance exhibits a high cached bandwidth of 132.41 GB/sec on small 16 KB blocks, dropping to 15.05 GB/sec read and 9.22 GB/sec write on larger 256 MB uncached blocks. Application benchmarks place Redis SET throughput at 2.24 million operations per second and static web serving at 3.69 GB/sec. Low-overhead inference tasks achieve 183.35 tokens per second for prompt processing on small 135M models, but medium 7B models fall to 11.35 tokens per second. The server provides a cost-efficient memory footprint for memory-intensive background tasks, low-traffic in-memory databases, and lightweight web serving, though it is not engineered for compute-heavy parallel workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-dense virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical Intel core with hyperthreading) and 16.0 GB of RAM on an x86_64 architecture. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached volumes for persistence. Supported hardware features include Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. In benchmarks, the instance yields average single-core throughput (Geekbench single-core score of 1640.0) alongside constrained multi-core performance due to its two-thread limit. Memory benchmarks indicate an uncached read bandwidth of 15.05 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 9.22 GB/sec. With its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, n4-highmem-2 is structurally aligned with small in-memory caching systems, lightweight databases, and memory-sensitive background microservices that do not require extensive parallel processing capacity.
